museums.content_summary: A cornerstone of South Carolina’s cultural life, the Columbia Museum of Art rewards art lovers with an engaging mix of European and American works, thoughtfully curated special exhibitions, and an intimate, easy-to-navigate gallery experience. Expect a strong regional perspective alongside bigger art-historical conversations—ideal for travelers who want substance without the sprawl of a mega-museum. With a lively downtown location and a calendar that often pairs art with talks and events, it’s a satisfying stop for both first-time visitors and repeat museumgoers.
museums.content_description:
**Columbia Museum of Art** is the kind of regional museum that surprises you: concentrated, carefully edited, and confident in its storytelling. Rather than overwhelming you with endless rooms, it offers a rewarding “close looking” experience—ideal for art enthusiasts who like to spend time with objects, labels, and curatorial context. Expect a core of European and American art—often spanning Old Master traditions through modern and contemporary work—anchored by rotating exhibitions that bring fresh themes and sharper focus to the permanent collection. For visitors, that means each trip can feel distinct, with new pairings, new scholarship, and new reasons to return.

The museum’s strengths lie in how it connects big art-history currents—think *portraiture*, *landscape*, and the evolution of *modernism*—to a regional setting and audience. The galleries tend to emphasize clarity and intimacy: you can move from room to room without losing the thread, and the scale invites comparison and discovery (a particular pleasure for travelers who want a meaningful museum visit in a manageable timeframe). Look out for interpretive materials and programming that deepen the visit—artist talks, family-friendly initiatives, and special events that often turn a museum stop into an evening plan.

Architecturally, **the building’s downtown presence** reinforces the museum’s role as a civic anchor: it feels like part of the city’s cultural fabric rather than a remote destination. For art-focused travelers, the experience is both polished and approachable—an excellent choice when you want strong exhibitions, a well-shaped collection, and the satisfaction of leaving with real visual memories, not just steps on a pedometer.
content_highlights: A tightly curated mix of European and American art that encourages slow looking and easy navigation
Rotating special exhibitions that regularly reshape the visit and spotlight new themes and artists
Galleries designed for an intimate viewing experience—ideal for comparing styles, techniques, and periods
A lively downtown cultural stop with events and programs that often complement exhibitions
A strong regional museum perspective: big art-history ideas presented with local relevance and accessibility

google_reviews.text: The exhibition for Keith Haring was pretty cool and brought back memories.  The African American museum was exceptional.  Both employees had great knowledge regarding the exhibition. No pictures of the Haring exhibition were allowed

The main exhibit on the second floor was closed, and the first-floor section was only partially accessible due to filming. While admission is free for South Carolina residents, out-of-state visitors are charged a $15 entry fee. Paying full price to see barely a quarter of the museum felt like a pretty raw deal.

We drove three hours to visit the Art Museum in Columbia, South Carolina, and it was a complete disappointment. We purchased our tickets on the first floor, and the receptionist never informed us that the second floor—where the main and most important artworks are located—was closed.

As a result, we were limited to viewing only a small selection of modern art on the first floor, which we did not enjoy at all. Had we been informed beforehand, we would never have paid for admission. When we questioned this afterward, the receptionist simply claimed that she “thought she had mentioned it,” which was not true.

I am active-duty military, and I normally do not leave reviews. However, this experience deserves to be shared. My family traveled from another country, and I had them make a long road trip specifically to visit this museum. Instead of a meaningful cultural experience, I ended up disappointing my family due to the museum’s lack of transparency.

We sacrificed time, money, and effort, and left feeling misled and frustrated. This experience felt like a waste of money.

One star. I strongly recommend asking very clearly what areas are open before purchasing tickets, or you may pay only to find out afterward that major sections are closed without any prior notice.

Nice museum. I enjoyed the Catawba pottery display; and the 12th/ 13th Century Italian triptych paintings, among other paintings. Expected more of the Jasper Johns exhibit, didn't find anything interesting there.  Collection sometimes questionable: why so many Hudson River School landscapes? and loads of Chinese objects that didn't really seem to appeal/ jell.  But glad I had the chance to visit, and Columbia is lucky to have this museum.
Keith Haring exhibit is great! Vivid colors with social commentary!  Definitely recommend!

museums.content_summary: The **Culture & Heritage Museums** in York County offer a captivating glimpse into the region's rich history across 14 beautiful acres of gardens. Visitors can explore a unique living collection and engage with informative wayside signs that illustrate the stories behind various historical sites. It's a perfect blend of nature and history, making it a must-visit destination for culture enthusiasts.
museums.content_description:
**Culture & Heritage Museums** invites you to step into the heart of York County’s storied past. Spanning 14 scenic acres, this history museum features a stunning collection of gardens, where visitors can meander through meticulously maintained paths and discover the natural splendor of the region. The gardens are not only a feast for the eyes but also serve as living history sites, each with wayside signs that share the fascinating stories of the land and its heritage. This immersive experience allows guests to connect with the environment while gaining insights into the preservation efforts that keep these stories alive.  

Inside the museum, you'll find an intriguing array of cultural exhibits that highlight the diverse history and traditions that have shaped York County. From artifacts that reflect early settlement life to displays showcasing the impact of industry and agriculture, every corner offers a unique narrative waiting to be uncovered. The architecture itself is a testament to the era it represents, featuring *colonial influences*, *Victorian touches*, and *modern adaptations* serving as backdrops to the rich collections. Whether you’re wandering through the lush gardens or exploring the diverse exhibits within the museum's walls, your visit promises an enriching journey through time—one that fosters a deep appreciation for both the cultural heritage and natural beauty of this remarkable region.
content_highlights: 14 acres of beautifully maintained gardens open to the public
Informative wayside signs detailing historical significance
Living collection that showcases local heritage efforts
Diverse exhibits covering early settlement to industrial history
Stunning architecture reflecting various historical styles

google_reviews.text: So unassuming but so worth it! We've been twice now and had such a great time wondering around and watching my 1 year old be in awe. Not super crowded, impressive exhibits, family friendly, and cheap! Can't wait to go back!

This is such a fabulous museum for all ages! Very easy to navigate, not too large, excellent displays and a marvelous planetarium!! They also have a fantastic museum shop and great staff!  A recent remodel has juts pushed this to 5 stars in my opinion!  Absolutely love it here!  SO great to have this gem "in the neighborhood"!

Overall we had a great experience! The museum is very clean. The staff was very helpful and friendly. This is one of the smaller, older museums. Nonetheless, it is great for younger children.  They have a small playroom for toddlers and infants. We did enjoy their planetarium as well!
I was impressed that in a not big town there is a rather impressive museum with a huge selection of exhibits and I was surprised that there was a planitarium and kid's play area.  We were satisfied.
Lots of animals to see. I feel like they should have had a live aquarium though I asked the worker if the animals was real and she explained me how it actually worked so that was very helpful

museums.content_summary: Discover the rich tapestry of Fort Mill's history at the **Fort Mill History Museum**. Dive into interactive exhibits and immersive displays that bring the past to life, making it a must-visit for history buffs and curious travelers alike.
museums.content_description:
**Fort Mill History Museum** serves as a captivating gateway into the historical narrative of Fort Mill, South Carolina. Nestled amid picturesque surroundings, this museum takes visitors on a journey through the town’s storied past, from its rich textile roots to the pivotal role it played in the local Civil War developments. With a focus on preserving and sharing the town's heritage, the museum offers a collection of exhibits that engage all ages, ensuring that history doesn't just educate but inspires as well. Visitors are invited to explore artifacts, photographs, and documents that bring to life the stories of the people who shaped this vibrant community.  

The architectural charm of **Fort Mill History Museum** itself tells a story. Housed in a historic building that reflects the locality’s character, the museum intricately blends historical preservation with innovative exhibit design. With enlightening wayside signs throughout its 14 acres, the museum grounds encourage outdoor exploration, allowing guests to soak in the scenic beauty while learning about significant events and the preservation efforts undertaken by Historic Columbia. As you wander through and partake in interactive displays, a sense of community pride and connection to the past unfurls, making each visit not only educational but emotionally resonant.
content_highlights: Interactive exhibits showcasing Fort Mill's textile industry
Preserved artifacts from the local Civil War history
Engaging wayside signs throughout the museum grounds
Beautifully landscaped gardens open to the public
Family-friendly activities that make history accessible

google_reviews.text: Wow. I can’t say enough good things about the programs, staff and volunteers at the Fort Mill History Museum. I recently became a member and the “members only” events and discounts are great! Yesterday, my husband and I, had the distinct pleasure of taking the Veterans Day tour in Unity Cemetery a few blocks away from the museum in Fort Mill SC. The morning session was for members only but due to the huge interest in her tours an afternoon tour was held for non-members for a small fee to support the museum. Krista B Huff has a passion for military history and has embraced the stories of some of Fort Mill’s bravest men who fought in WWI and WWII. The 45 minute tour was pedestrian friendly with 3 dedicated stops, complete with photos of each man, loaned artifacts, and a pin as a parting gift. The tour even included a number of out of town relatives of some of the men highlighted. This was such an incredibly important and memorable experience. Krista indicated that she is already working on a new program for Memorial Day and Veterans Day 2026. Stay tuned.
Visited 11/25/22. Very kind gentleman gave us a tour and talked about the history of how Fort Mill came to be. Free but appreciates donations. Enjoyed!

Overview:
If you’re looking for a town treasure, look no further and be sure to check out the Fort Mill History Museum. Quaint and humble, this site speaks softly and carries a big stick of greatness!

Parking:
Two primary locations, the first closest is behind the building, coming from Confederate St, onto Main St you’ll find “hidden” parking behind the museum. The second closest is in the front across the street at the Organic Kitchen’s parking lot.

Attractions:
Multiple rooms with several artifacts and written stories about various locations and people from Fort Mill, namely the White and Springs families, as well as several others. The feeling you get from realizing the rich history of the town really provides a new level of appreciation and awareness. There’s also a great gift shop with books, ornaments, and hand made tributes to some of the town’s iconic locations.

Staff:
Extremely knowledgeable and welcoming, this  group is full of class and personality. From the first greeting you knew you were in for a good time. Several stories can be shared and rich explanations that lead to further discoveries. So much can be said about the volunteer staff there, but it sums up to calling them close friends, if not, family. You may meet David, Pat, Sheila or  other fantastic volunteer hosts.

Price:
Free admission which can’t be beat. Of course it’s always good to support the museums cause by way of monetary donations, filling in the visitor registration card, or making purchases of the many unique gifts.

Bottom Line:
Highly recommended that you make a stop to get familiar with the town and its rich history. The new appreciations you’ll have are priceless and you may make a new friend or two.
This place is a great stop for local history and it comes with a free very informative tour. David was very kind and also told us they have ghost tours in October. Very cool

What a wonderful representation of the history of our town. I truly enjoyed walking through and listening to the guided tour. It was entertaining and educational. I highly recommend this for natives and newcomers!!

Explore 14 acres of lush greenery and captivating wayside signs that weave together the stories of Columbia's heritage, making it an enriching stop for history enthusiasts and nature lovers alike.
museums.content_description: **Historic Columbia** is not just a museum; it is a vibrant celebration of the city's history, culture, and natural beauty. Spread across 14 acres of meticulously maintained gardens, visitors can wander through scenic landscapes that tell the story of Columbia's evolution and community spirit. The gardens, which are free to the public seven days a week, offer a tranquil setting for reflection and education, highlighting the importance of historic preservation through various living collections. Each corner reveals a unique aspect of the area's heritage, and the informative wayside signs provide insightful context that enriches the visitor experience. Here, history isn't confined to walls; it flourishes in the outdoors.  *Explore the flora that has roots reaching back to the early settlers and enjoy the tranquil sound of water features harmonizing with the surrounding environment.*   As you stroll, look for the native plants that were essential to the local economy and cultural practices, highlighting the intrinsic link between nature and history.  *Engage with our educational initiatives that empower visitors with knowledge about preservation and the stories that form the backbone of our community's identity.*  **Historic Columbia**'s fusion of nature and heritage serves as a reminder of the importance of these spaces and their role in maintaining a connection with our past.  *The experience culminates in a deeper appreciation for the stories that have shaped this remarkable place.*
content_highlights: 14 acres of meticulously maintained gardens
Informative wayside signs detailing local history
Free entry for public to explore the grounds
Unique living collections showcasing historical flora
Educational initiatives focused on preservation and community heritage

google_reviews.text: Historic Columbia, you ought to be ashamed of yourself! I came from thousands of miles away to look at the black history of this city and believe me you all did a horrible job which means you're still showing your Confederate side. What do I mean by this?? For example, I went to the tourist office to get information on the African-American landmarks.  I received a haphazard map that's poorly marked and when I took it to Main Street to try to find these places, it was all vague. The parking meters were labeled better. And let's not go into detail about the fact that a United States President gave a historic speech prior to launching his campaign and winning the presidency at Benedict College. Yes there's no mention of that. Why? Because it was held at an auditorium that was segregated and is the only standing example of a segregated auditorium in these United States. Should I mention that if I drove around randomly and hopefully found some signs, I could learn a little bit about the merchants that first created businesses to sell to African Americans.  Where is the book about the markers? They have numbers but where can I find the list of all of them together so I know where they are? And should I remind you that Waverly Street was a proud neighborhood built for African Americans that made a significant contribution to the city because they were considered middle class.  I'm sure you know that The Honorable Major Charity Adams ( who risked the lives of many to make sure that our American servicemen, particularly the white servicemen, received their mail during WW2)  lived in this area and Hollywood thought that her contribution to America was so significant that they selected one of the premier movie stars (Kerry Washington- of Scandal And many other movie/tv fame) to play her in the movie Six Triple 8?? There are historic black college is here too- It's an embarrassment. They're not even listed in your brochures and many, many contributions to American society were made by scholars that attended these schools. I think I'll stop and not go on and on. You know what you have here. You just don't want anyone else to know and that's a damn shame....you're taking away a strong part of American history that you should be proud of. You're sweeping it under the rug and showing your hind side. Please, when people go to the tourist office after traveling thousands of miles, the least you could do is have one brochure that lets the truth be known.   By the way, we already know because it's in US history now and it's online everywhere but we should not have to gather it up ourselves and try to figure it out when we get here. You all are an embarrassment to society And the American people. And this intolerance that you have against the history that you made and misused should be turned around and designed to be the pride of America as it helped to transform this country into the place it is now.
Wonderful tour of Hampton Preston AND Robert Mills house. Holiday tour so the homes were decorated according to the time period. Our guide Shawn, was outstanding.

The Mann-Simons site is set up as a self-guided experience, so it seems unnecessary to require visitors to pay for a tour guide and drive around the small neighborhood in their own vehicles. It would be much more convenient if the home had open house hours, allowing guests to explore at their own pace rather than being required to follow a structured tour—especially if they’re only interested in one of the houses. While the exhibits consist mostly of videos and informational signs, the history itself is interesting. Overall, I’m glad to have visited the Mann-Simons house, but I was disappointed in the way the tour was structured.

Historic Columbia and their team are wonderful!!  I had correspondences with John, Kat and Jeff - they were all phenomenal.  We were looking for a history tour to do because we were stopping in Columbia for a night and hadn't explored it.  There were many wonderful sites to see on their website, but we just wanted an overview of the city and to learn more about the history - like we do in most cities we visit.

We didn't see one online, but reached out and they connected us with one of their volunteers - Jeff P. - he did a wonderful tour and had tons of pictures from years back.  We could clearly tell he's passionate about what he does.

Kat was kind enough to suggest some wonderful restaurants and local spots to try out while we were in!!

We truly loved our experience of Historic (and beautiful) Columbia.  Thank you again, John, Kat and Jeff for making our trip so special!!

Do not just show up up here. Check the website to see if you can figure out when and how to visit some of the historic homes and gardens. Or contact them to ask... it definitely requires more planning ahead than I like to do on vacation. On your adventure, you can hope to learn about Columbia while you see architectural styles spanning three centuries. Or maybe you just wander through the neighborhood admiring the old homes on your own.

With its stunning collections and tranquil gardens, it offers a vivid glimpse into South Carolina's rich heritage and preservation efforts, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring the state's past.
museums.content_description:
**The South Carolina Historical Society Museum** serves as a beacon of historical preservation in the charming city of Charleston. Nestled within 14 acres of beautifully maintained gardens, this museum invites visitors to embark on a journey through time, uncovering the storied past of America's Palmetto State. The grounds are adorned with wayside signs that illuminate key historical moments and the ongoing efforts to safeguard South Carolina's cultural legacy. This gentle blend of nature and history creates an experience that is both educational and serene.  

The museum's collection is captivating, featuring artifacts that span centuries of South Carolina's history. From colonial documents to modern memorabilia, each piece tells a story of the people and events that shaped the state. The architecture of the museum itself reflects the style of the eras it showcases, providing a visual feast that enhances the narrative of the exhibitions. Visitors can delve into various exhibits and appreciate the craftsmanship of the artifacts alongside the lush backdrop of gardens that change with the seasons. Exploring this unique space is not just about viewing history; it’s about feeling connected to it through its preservation efforts and the natural beauty surrounding you.
content_highlights: Stunning 14 acres of gardens open to the public
Informative wayside signs detailing preservation efforts
Vast collection of historical artifacts spanning centuries
Architectural beauty reflecting South Carolina's history
Serene environment for relaxed exploration and learning

google_reviews.text: A great way to learn about SC history. From the greeter at the front door to the exhibits to the historic building that houses everything, it's a must do for history buffs.

We had a great welcome to the museum by Mitchel! I enjoyed the exhibits and exploring the history of the building. This is definitely a must stop if you visit Charleston. I love the interior design of the building, especially the staircase. There is a public parking garage close by, an easy 2 minute walk. Purchase your tickets when you walk in, directly from the museum - admission is $1 per person.
Fantastic establishment with some facinating South Carolina history. The staff is very kind and welcoming. Building and grounds are extremely well kept. Will definitely go back to visit!

We were lucky to visit on $1 admission day.
The volunteer was extremely helpful with expectations of the museum.
It took us around 1-1:30 hour to visit. If you have the time, make sure you visit. The gift stop had amazing prices on individual prints. $10 each.

This was a great museum. I went on Saturday in February 2026. The gentleman running the counter on Valentine’s Day was great. I’m a teacher myself. I absolutely and thoroughly enjoyed walking this place and talking to the gentleman.

museums.content_summary: The **South Carolina State Museum** is a cultural treasure trove located in Columbia, offering a captivating exploration of the state's history, art, and science. With its diverse collections and engaging exhibits, this museum provides a unique opportunity for visitors to discover the rich heritage and natural wonders of South Carolina all under one roof.
museums.content_description: **South Carolina State Museum** stands as a beacon of heritage and learning, nestled in the heart of Columbia. Spanning **four floors** and featuring **art, history, natural history**, and **science exhibits**, this museum is the largest in the state, making it a must-visit destination for anyone looking to immerse themselves in the diverse narratives that shape South Carolina. From *Native American artifacts* to **historic artifacts** of the American Revolution, each exhibit offers a glimpse into the rich past of the Palmetto State. The museum's dedication to preserving and interpreting these stories makes it an important educational institution for residents and travelers alike.  Additionally, the stunning **restoration of the historic Columbia Mill** adds to the museum's charm and visual appeal.  Visitors can marvel at this architectural gem as they explore the collections within.  Beyond the exhibits, the museum also hosts special programs, workshops, and events that invite community engagement and enrich the visitor experience.  Whether you're interested in the region's *ecological diversity* or the vibrant *artistic movements* that have flourished here, there's something for everyone at the **South Carolina State Museum**.  Don't forget to take advantage of the beautifully landscaped **gardens spanning 14 acres**, offering serene spots for reflection and a chance to appreciate the natural beauty surrounding the museum.  A visit here is not just about viewing exhibits; it's an invitation to connect with the essence of South Carolina and its spirited past.  Experience history, immerse yourself in art, and find inspiration in the stories waiting to be discovered.
content_highlights: Largest collection of historical artifacts in South Carolina
Engaging science and natural history exhibits
Restored historic Columbia Mill showcased within the museum
14 acres of beautifully landscaped gardens
Dynamic programs and community events throughout the year

google_reviews.text: Four floor, South Carolina historically oriented museum. Interesting progression from prehistoric to present. I suggest grabbing one of the free maps to help you navigate the somewhat twisty turny display routes. There are two "movie" type exhibits. One, we didn't view said it was a 4D experience. The other was the planetarium and we enjoyed a presentation on the aurora borealis.

This was my first time visiting the South Carolina State Museum and I really enjoyed it. The staff were very friendly. The museum has four floors with exhibits on state history, natural history, science, and art. I especially loved the natural history and astronomy areas. The South Carolina history section was very interesting too. The art section is small but beautiful. The Science of the Sound exhibit was very informative and had many interactive activities, which are great for kids. The military museum is separate, but it can be accessed through the museum admission area. We watched a planetarium show that was fun and educational. They also offer 4D movies, but I did not have enough time to see one. I will definitely come back again.

Fabulous museum which far exceeded my expectations.  Four floors of displays on state history, natural history, science, and art.  We saw one of the 4D movies which were fun, but really short (less than 15 minutes).  They have a new Revolutionary War exhibit under construction which should be open by mid 2026 for the 250th anniversary.  The scale replica of the CSS Huntley is particularly interesting to see.

I want to say if you buy tickets online, you will still have to wait in a ticket purchase line for your ticket to be scanned so you can be admitted into the museum. I thought this was very inefficient and defeated the purpose of buying online. also, there is a bit of a discount when you purchase your tickets in person.

now the actual museum itself was overall okay. I think this museum is great for families with young children and schools. while the things you see are interesting, a lot of interactive features were broken and/or faulty. there was currently construction for a new exhibit about the American revolution which I think would be very interesting to see.

we visited almost everything except for the confederate museum. we simply were just tired and skipped out on that section. we were very disappointed to see a purchased piece of artwork tacked up with cheap nails that punctured the piece. it's just felt disrespectful to the artwork and the artist especially since it was such a masterful piece. the heroes and villains exhibit was amazing, but I recommend getting a later entry as midday typically is very busy. we also had tickets to the planetarium and saw the show arora which was lovely. I do recommend seeing that show early in your day as it will lull you to want to sleep. it also ends with you walking towards the beginning of the museum.

I hope this was illuminating and provided you with any information you needed to know. like I said, the museum was overall okay.

This was my first visit to the South Carolina State Museum, and I was genuinely impressed. There was so much to see, and everything was laid out in a way that made it easy and enjoyable to explore. I loved the variety of exhibits, history, science, and art which kept the experience interesting the entire time. My absolute favorite part was the Heroes and Villains exhibit. Seeing the Disney costumes up close was honestly magical, the details, textures, and craftsmanship were far more impressive in person than I expected. For a first visit, it exceeded my expectations, and I’m already looking forward to coming back again.

museums.content_description: **Sumter County Gallery of Art** invites visitors to embark on a captivating journey through time, showcasing the rich historical narrative of Sumter and its surrounding area. The gallery is not just a museum; it’s a bridge connecting the stories of diverse eras through stunning *artistic* installations and compelling exhibits. From regional artwork to historical artifacts, each piece has been thoughtfully selected to reflect the vibrant cultural tapestry of the region. The museum offers a space where visitors can discover the impact of local artists and historical figures on the broader canvas of South Carolina's art scene. Throughout the gallery, guests will find opportunities to engage with both contemporary and historical contexts, making each visit unique and enlightening.  Often rotating exhibitions ensure there’s always something new to discover, while wayside signs and informative placards deepen the learning experience.  The ambiance is inviting; taking a leisurely stroll through the exhibits offers a chance for reflection and inspiration, ideal for art aficionados and casual visitors alike.  Moreover, the gallery often hosts events such as workshops, talks, and community gatherings, fostering a friendly atmosphere where creativity flourishes.  Whether you are an art lover seeking fresh inspiration or a history buff hungry for local stories, the **Sumter County Gallery of Art** promises a rewarding experience that highlights the beauty of cultural heritage.  For an enriching afternoon, uncover the treasures of this charming locale and enjoy a moment of connection with the artistry that embodies Sumter’s soul.
content_highlights: Diverse collection of local artwork reflecting regional history
Engaging rotating exhibitions featuring contemporary artists
Thoughtfully curated historical artifacts from Sumter County
Interactive programs and community events that foster local engagement
Beautiful setting that encourages exploration and reflection in the gallery

google_reviews.text: Pleasant spot for changing exhibitions.   I enjoyed the show on display by an Asian woman artist: Jiha Moon, and her "A Mad Tea Party."  Various media, from wall hangings and masks to the actual "tea party" create an interesting and evocative visual experience.
I took my children, we enjoy art. This spot has some really nice pieces and art classes for people from like 6 to adult.
A small gallery with lovely exhibitions. I'm a big fan of those galleries that showcase local artists and artisans, and this gallery does that. The staff is warm and friendly. Highly recommend!
A hidden gem in Sumter and for the whole state of South Carolina.  A diverse range of artists have their work shown here.  Very helpful and inviting staff.

My husband and I signed up for a pottery class and had THE BEST time! Rachel and Zoe (sp?) were our instructors and I loved every minute of it! I was 32 weeks pregnant when the class started and my husband had just crushed his finger in a work accident but they made it the best experience. I would recommend taking any class if they are half as good as this one!

museums.content_summary: The Sumter County Museum offers an immersive experience into the rich history and culture of Sumter, South Carolina. With engaging exhibits, beautiful gardens, and hands-on activities, this museum is a treasure trove for history enthusiasts and families alike, making it a must-visit on your next trip.
museums.content_description:
**Sumter County Museum** serves as a vibrant gateway into the heart of South Carolina's history. Nestled in a picturesque landscape, it stands out as a center of learning, exploration, and cultural heritage. Visitors will find themselves captivated by the museum's curated exhibits that highlight crucial aspects of local history, including the region's role in the Civil War, its agricultural roots, and the colorful narratives of its diverse inhabitants. The museum's layout encourages exploration, making it as much a journey through time as it is a collection of artifacts.  

The *architecture* of the museum itself is a blend of historical charm and modern design, providing a backdrop that complements the story it tells. With interactive exhibits, living history demonstrations, and special events, visitors will not only observe but also engage with the past. The museum's outdoor gardens—spanning 14 acres—add to the enchanting experience, allowing guests to stroll through lush paths and discover wayside signs that unravel the history of the land and its preservation efforts. Furthermore, the inclusion of community events fosters a sense of connection to Sumter, making each visit unique. Don't miss the chance to uncover the hidden gems of **Sumter County Museum**!
content_highlights: Engaging exhibits on local Civil War history
Interactive experiences for families and children
Beautifully landscaped gardens for serene exploration
Focus on Sumter's agricultural heritage and local culture
Hands-on activities that allow visitors to experience history live

google_reviews.text: Great history of the house and its owners as it relates to the development of the community. A short tour is given at the beginning to give an overview and then you are left to peruse the house and grounds.  The house is currently displaying Williams furniture from one of the owner's company as well as many items from that era. There is a very nice display of old buildings on the property which are filled with items used in the past. Everything has been well maintained.

We had our wedding at the museum and it was the perfect garden gala event! The price cannot be beat and the staff is very helpful. It’s a perfect location. We had around 130 guests and felt like we had plenty of room!

Went to the museum for the first time since attending Bates Middle School😅😅😅. It’s a nice little trip to learn some history of foundation of our home.  For only $5, get out there and experience what they have to offer.  The gentleman who greeted me had a wealth of knowledge and definitely made the experience a fruitful one!

Love learning more about our local history. This site has great information, some historical gadgets I had never seen before and staff was knowledgeable about the founders and their heritage. Very much enjoyed!

The Sumter Co. Genealogical Society is in the basement of the museum in the front of the house. I went there to find some of my ancestors who faught in the Rev War. I want to join the DAR group. Found them in books from the 1770s. They have the whole East Coast of books from the early 1770s. So if you are looking for someone, they might have it. There is a $20 non-member fee per day.  I asked why and the man said, they are all volunteers and it's just a way to get a bit of funding to help with daily operations. I'm fine with that. They have books and local maps for sale also. Museum back country area is what Sumter Co would have look like in the 1700’s. They have Back County days 2 times a year and other events throughout the year. Pirate day is a fun one in June. Beautiful place for weddings and other events. Beautiful place to take pictures also.
They also have costumes for rent.

museums.content_summary: The Gibbs Museum of Art is a treasure nestled in the heart of Charleston, showcasing unparalleled collections of American art. With a focus on both historic and contemporary pieces, visitors can immerse themselves in the vibrant artistic narrative of the region. Unique exhibits, combined with the serene gardens, make this museum a must-visit for anyone exploring Charleston.
museums.content_description:
**The Gibbs Museum of Art** represents a confluence of artistic expression and historical preservation, set amidst the charming backdrop of Charleston. Founded on the principles of cultivation and appreciation of American art, this museum houses a diverse collection that spans multiple centuries. Visitors will encounter stunning works that reflect the artistic evolution and cultural richness of the South, from traditional portraiture to innovative modern pieces that challenge perceptions and inspire dialogue. The curated collections include masterworks by renowned artists, American folk art, and pieces that highlight local Charleston narratives, making it a vital part of South Carolina's artistic heritage.  

The museum itself is an architectural gem that complements its collections beautifully. The historic building is surrounded by 14 acres of gardens, where winding paths lead you to breathtaking landscapes and tranquil spots for reflection. Visitors are encouraged to explore the outdoor installations and wayside signs that offer insights into both the art and the historical significance of this beautiful setting. Spend an afternoon leisurely wandering through galleries and gardens, immersing yourself in the stories behind the art and the environment that fostered such creativity. The **Gibbs Museum of Art** not only showcases art but invites individuals to engage with the history and natural beauty that Charleston offers.
content_highlights: Diverse collections showcasing American art from various periods
Beautifully landscaped 14-acre garden for relaxation and exploration
Unique outdoor installations enhancing the visitor experience
Opportunities to learn about the history of the region through art
Engaging educational programs and exhibitions for all ages

google_reviews.text: We went on a Wednesday,  when they offer free admission.  But would have gladly paid. The space itself is stunningly beautiful. Both the permanent and special exhibitions were wonderful.  There permanent (mostly) South Carolina themed exhibition was varied and beautifully done. And the the current special exhibit are the Etchings of Rembrandt.  Fantastic! I had never seen them before and really enjoyed learning about the process of etchings, the references and subjects he used, including himself, and some of the other artists who used the same technique and/or emulated him, like Picasso and Whistler.

Really beautiful building with a wonderful permanent collection. The current rotating exhibition was on Harriet Tubman and was exceptionally well done. It was a nice combination of 2D art, video, and sculpture/artifact.

We went during the Wednesday late hours (5-8pm) with free admission but I think it would have been well worth the $15 per person admission.
Enjoyed the Rembrandt exhibit and other works of art. It is a fairly small art museum and we were able to navigate it in about 2 hours.

We went with my husband’s family on a Sunday, just trying to find something to do on a rainy day. I saw in the comments that it was free—turns out, nope! It’s actually $14 a person.

That said, the place is super pretty, really well kept, and bigger than I expected. The art is awesome—lots of pieces inspired by Charleston’s landscape and vibe, which I loved.

Honestly, the price isn’t bad. If you’re into art, it’s definitely worth checking out!

wonderful time exploring three floors of art. enjoyed the Rembrandt etchings exhibition and especially the permanent collection. outstanding collection and so approachable/accessible in the heart of Charleston.

museums.content_summary: Charleston’s Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art is a must for art lovers who want to experience the city’s living creative pulse. Rather than a permanent collection, the Halsey shines through carefully curated, rotating exhibitions that spotlight contemporary artists and urgent ideas. Expect an intimate, gallery-forward visit—ideal for returning multiple times—where the emphasis is on discovery, conversation, and seeing what’s happening in contemporary art right now in the Lowcountry and beyond.
museums.content_description:
**Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art** offers a focused, contemporary counterpoint to Charleston’s historic streetscapes—a place where you come to see *now*, not a fixed canon. As a non-collecting institution, its strength is curatorial: a steady cadence of rotating exhibitions that can move from emerging voices to nationally recognized artists, often with thoughtful wall texts and programming that invite close looking. For travelers building an art itinerary, the Halsey is especially rewarding because every visit feels current—what’s on view changes, and with it the conversation around materials, images, and ideas.

The visitor experience is gallery-centered and deliberately uncluttered: you’ll spend your time with the work, not navigating crowds or encyclopedic displays. Expect to encounter contemporary practices across **painting, photography, video, installation, and conceptual approaches**, frequently framed in ways that resonate with Charleston’s cultural landscape without being limited by it. If you’re the kind of museumgoer who loves reading labels, attending talks, or catching an opening, this is a place that rewards curiosity.

Plan to check the exhibition calendar before you go, then give yourself time to linger—contemporary art here often reveals itself through detail, process, and context. The Halsey is best experienced as a repeat stop: return on a later day (or a future trip) and you’ll find an entirely different show, effectively turning one museum into many.
content_highlights: Rotating contemporary exhibitions (no permanent collection), so each visit offers new work and new ideas
Curator-led, research-driven shows spanning painting, photography, video, and installation
A strong “right now” complement to Charleston’s historic museums—ideal for travelers seeking contemporary perspectives
Programming that deepens engagement: talks, openings, and interpretive materials (check current schedule)
An intimate, gallery-first experience designed for slow looking and close attention to individual works

google_reviews.text: The main building houses the excellent gallery space as well as exhibit space in the hallways - all of it was worth viewing. This is located on the College of Charleston’s campus and is free to the public but a donation is suggested. We enjoyed the art and would definitely revisit when we are in Charleston.

An incredibly interesting art museum. Highly recommend going to the back to see both short videos about the artists/displays. I was particularly intrigued by the discussion and artistic display of caodaism.

A highlight of our Charleston visit. Free to visit and admire the wonders of modern artists with an international and native points of perception.
Also, to learn about every aspect of creativity in the dedicated library.
Left inspired and grateful to diversity of self-expression.
Highly recommend.

Small but mighty exhibits provided for the can't be beaten price of free. This isn't a huge museum, so you won't be spending a whole afternoon here, but it's a great option to stop in, get out of the heat, and see something new. If I lived in the area I would absolutely come back as the exhibits change regularly.

Impressive little gallery where you can browse a variety of student work, read the artist statements, and even purchase works in miniature from an Artomat vending machine. You'll also find a small biblioteca tucked away within the main gallery space; I wish we'd had more time to peruse it.

The Namsa Leuba exhibition, Crossed Looks, was an explosion of powerful and vibrant images, and there's a sort of grotto where you can watch a short video about the artist and her work.

We'll be back in January for Dyani White Hawk. This place is clearly doing great things in the community .

museums.content_summary: Discover the rich military heritage of South Carolina at the **Confederate Relic Room & Military Museum** in Columbia. With a unique collection of artifacts, uniforms, and memorabilia, this museum offers an immersive experience into the state's Civil War history, making it an invaluable stop for history buffs and curious travelers alike.
museums.content_description:
**The South Carolina Confederate Relic Room & Military Museum** is a treasure trove of military history located in the heart of Columbia. Established to honor South Carolina's military contributions, this museum houses a remarkable collection of artifacts from the American Civil War era to modern military conflicts. Visitors will find themselves enveloped in stories that highlight the bravery and sacrifice of South Carolinians through time. The museum's commitment to preserving and presenting these pieces makes it a vital proof of the state’s rich history.  

As you explore the museum, you'll encounter everything from authentic Confederate uniforms to battle flags and weapons, each telling a story of valor and commitment. The architecture of the museum itself is inviting, with spacious galleries designed to enhance the visitor experience, ensuring that exhibits are engaging and accessible. Interactive displays make it easier for guests to connect with the past, while well-curated narratives provide context for the artifacts at hand. 

In addition to permanent exhibits, the museum hosts special events and educational programs, inviting visitors of all ages to deepen their understanding of military history. Whether you're a local, a history enthusiast, or a tourist looking for a unique glimpse into the past, the **Confederate Relic Room & Military Museum** is a must-visit destination that promises an enlightening experience you won't forget.
content_highlights: Extensive collection of Civil War artifacts
Authentic Confederate uniforms and military ephemera
Interactive displays for a hands-on learning experience
Educational programs and special exhibits
Rich insights into South Carolina's military legacy

google_reviews.text: The museum has been renovated and is now open again. It’s separate from the SC State Museum, so be sure to check hours and prices before you go (state museum and Confederate museum are two separate entry fees). There are two main displays at this point - the Vietnam war display and the “other wars” (primarily civil but a couple sections on revolutionary, ww2, desert storm). These aren’t big displays, but they’re interesting and give more of a human feel to these wars since most of the items are personal (letters to home, personal firearms, ways people were killed in action, etc).

My husband and I had an awesome time, we learned even more about the history of South Carolina and American history, I recommend that you show up early because it takes a good while to go through the museum and read the things posted about this history.

This was a fun museum and my fiance and I really enjoyed checking out all the exhibits. The museum itself is comprised of 4 separate stories, each story containing 3-5 different exhibits. There are also there different shows you can attend if you get the "Master Explorer Ticket" which cost approximately $12 per adult including a 4D show, a planetarium show, and an exhibit show. It was a fun day and we really enjoyed our experience. The ONLY reason this is getting 3 stars is due to my experiences with museum trips in cities such as San Diego, Washington D.C., and Norfolk which are vastly larger as would be expected.
Drove over 4 hours each way to attend the Revolutionary War day, not disappointed!  Great volunteers and workers!

Very nice museum. My kids enjoyed it. Best part of it is that it was only 1$ for entrance per person. So many things to look at, will definitely be going back soon to finish looking at everything this museum has to offer!

museums.content_summary: Tucked inside Bob Jones University, the Bob Jones University Museum & Gallery is one of the Southeast’s most surprising stops for old-master painting and European devotional art. Its compact scale makes it easy to visit without fatigue, yet the galleries reward close looking with richly crafted Renaissance and Baroque works, luminous altarpiece imagery, and strong representation of 19th‑century academic and salon traditions. For art lovers in Greenville, it’s a focused, atmospheric museum experience with real aesthetic punch.
museums.content_description:
**Bob Jones University Museum & Gallery** offers an unexpectedly concentrated encounter with European art, especially painting and religious imagery, presented in a setting designed for careful, quiet looking. While not a sprawling encyclopedic institution, it excels as a **teaching museum**—the kind of place where you can stand close to a panel painting, trace the finesse of glazing in an oil work, and notice how artists orchestrate light, gesture, and symbolism. Expect strengths in *Renaissance* and *Baroque* sensibilities—dramatic contrasts, devotional intensity, and refined craftsmanship—alongside later European works that reflect *academic* polish and narrative clarity.

The museum’s appeal is also experiential: the galleries tend to be **intimate and legible**, so you can move chronologically and thematically without feeling rushed. For travelers, that means it pairs well with a day in Greenville—an energizing, art-forward stop that complements the city’s food and walkable downtown. Architecturally, you’re visiting a campus museum rather than a landmark “starchitect” building, but that works in its favor: the focus stays on the objects, with controlled lighting and a calm viewing rhythm.

Plan to linger on the museum’s European painting and devotional objects, where composition, surface, and iconography invite slow reading. Even if you’re not a specialist in *Christian iconography*, the works offer a direct line into the visual language that shaped Western art for centuries—ideal for enthusiasts who enjoy connecting technique to meaning and leaving with a sharper eye.
content_highlights: Compact European-focused galleries that reward close, unhurried looking
Strong presence of Renaissance- and Baroque-inspired devotional imagery and old-master traditions
Opportunities to study technique up close—glazing, chiaroscuro, and narrative composition
A teaching-museum atmosphere: quiet, focused spaces suited to attentive viewing
Easy to combine with a Greenville itinerary thanks to the museum’s manageable scale and campus setting

google_reviews.text: The gallery contains an impressive collection of Christian art. A large part of the collection is centered on 14th to 19th century art and icons from the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches. Though closed to the public since 2017, their galleries are still available to view online, which is wonderful to behold.

The Museum and Gallery has broadened my horizons and given me a love for art that I never had before. Not only is the artwork incredible, but the staff is such a joy to be around. I have learned so much from the M&G staff there and appreciate their sweet spirit and positive attitude. It really creates a relaxing environment (or makes even the busiest day a joyful experience). If you have not gone, please make it a point to go! Be ready to have your mind, heart, and soul challenged, as is their mission. In my personal experience, art has the power to transform your way of looking at things. Be prepared for truth to come alive in a most unusual way. Thank you, M&G for all you do.

This is my favorite museum of European Christian art the last millennium in the entire state and there is nowhere I have seen this art that it's so holy and beautiful. reminds me of my Treasures in Heaven and everyone should see this Museum .people would realize that Jesus Christ is Lord they could see this museum actually wish I could start a charity that would give transportation and Museum these so that old people and people who are dying of cancer and deadly diseases could go to these museums and see their Treasures in Heaven and then maybe they wouldn't be afraid of dying

I have lots of good memories of this place. I was in charge of *lightly and carefully* cleaning the works of art. I was also a gallery guard. This was around 79 to 83. The staff were very friendly and professional. I hope the gallery reopens soon!

At end of our guard shift we always had to search our section for "bombs and bodies". I remember also that the ladies, especially Mrs. Poindexter, trying to catch us in the act of sitting down on the job.

One time Dr. Bob Jr. saw me on a ladder going over a huge painting with a cleaning brush  (I think it was The Ascension, Gustave Dore) and expressed concern downstairs but was told I was being careful.

A phenomenal collection, viewing it is similar to experiencing Biltmore House: I don't believe it's possible to appreciate it all in one visit because your brain becomes desensitized to the awe after a few hours and yet there's still so much more to see.
HIGHLY RECOMMEND you add the Living Gallery production to your bucket list.

Visitors step into a *dynamic space* where *history comes alive*, showcasing everything from the early Native American cultures to the modernization of the area in the 20th century. As you wander through the thoughtfully curated galleries, you will encounter *immersive displays*, compelling narratives, and even digital interactive stations that invite you to delve deeper into the past. The **Upcountry History Museum** also offers a variety of community programs and temporary exhibitions, ensuring that there is always something new to learn and discover. google_reviews.text: Its a small and quaint museum,  but it has a really nice charm. And as a plus they dont charge extra for the visiting exhibits like some larger museums do. My mom and I really enjoyed it and will visit again.
Absolutely amazing museum! Super friendly staff and wonderful exhibits! Adorable giftshop with fun items. Great history of the area and of SC. We loved it so much!
Very nice local museum with interesting permanent exhibits and very interesting rotating temporary exhibits.

Friendly staff. Decent price or free with library pass that can be borrowed. Local history and South Carolina history. Interactive and highly educational. My kids enjoyed the little scavenger hunt. It was fun to see how quickly the kids could work in the cotton factory.  We really enjoyed the D-day exhibit and Lady Bird Johnson dresses! Cons

google_reviews.text: Amazing place, kind staff, beautiful art work. This place is sure to please the art filled heart. My little humans have adored each class they have and we cant stop singing them up. The memberships are such great prices and you support local art and education.  Highly recommend you so by if you have the time. If you love to work with pottery, they have a studio as well!!!

This is a super cute museum with a gift shop, small library and 2 exhibit rooms. They have free entry, but a donation is encouraged. While the gallery rooms are small they are very well laid out, well lit, and give you lots of space to walk around and admire the artwork. The gift shop has great Options if you're looking for work from local artists, a souvenir, or something for the art lover you know.

I am happy we decided to spend time in the museum. The artwork is beautiful and I enjoyed the juried collection, of high school students' artwork. Lots of artistic talent !! It was a nice afternoon!! Also had to snap a pic in front of the 'Trash Octopus' !

What a lovely little art museum/gallery! Who knew Myrtle Beach had such a gem. The three current exhibits when I visited were well curated and each one very interesting. I especially enjoyed the exhibit of local fiber artist, Joann Morgan's Memorial Quilts.

Great little art museum. They had the cultural currency and Paul Yanko exhibits upstairs and downstairs. It is a very small museum but definitely worth a visit. Donations are appreciated and a gift shop with local artists. They also had a window room with tea and biscuits for $1 each.
